Looking at this question about C. elegans heat stress response in adr-1 and adr-2 mutants:

ADR-1 and ADR-2 are nuclear receptors in C. elegans that play important roles in thermotolerance. Studies on these mutants exposed to heat stress (36°C for 6 hours) with subsequent recovery at 20°C show that these mutants have significantly reduced thermotolerance compared to wild-type worms.

The single mutants (adr-1(-) and adr-2(-)) show increased heat sensitivity, and the double mutant (adr-1(-);adr-2(-)) shows the most dramatic increase in mortality. Under these specific conditions (36°C for 6 hours, 14h recovery at 20°C), these mutants show approximately 80% mortality.

[ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
